failure_modes: Orthogonal readout changes are attributable to assay interference from formulation excipients or buffer incompatibility rather than true loss of membrane integrity or protected cargo (false positive stability failure).

Assay platform or capture reagents fail to perform consistently across formulation matrices or lots (reagent incompatibility or lot‑to‑lot assay variability), making qualitative pass/fail non‑reproducible.
Insufficient material yield from ≥3 independent production lots to support protected multi‑omic profiling across the full exposure matrix, leading to underpowered or non‑generalizable conclusions.

Orthogonal signatures are preserved after stressors but intact EVs are still cleared or trapped in the administration route (e.g., retained in nasal cavity) or fail to reach target tissue in larger species — producing false assurance of in vivo deliverability (false negative translational prediction).

Bulk particle measures remain unchanged because methods detect membrane fragments or non‑vesicular particles, so particle:protein ratios or particle peaks mislead stability assessments when protected cargo is depleted or absent.

Observed attribute changes are small, inconsistent across lots, or occur only under extreme conditions, preventing definition of actionable/clinically relevant acceptance envelopes (unmeasurable/undifferentiated outcome).

Orthogonal attributes identified in the MSC‑derived, small‑animal contexts do not generalize to the intended clinical formulation/device or scale‑up processes, necessitating rework of CMC strategy late in development.
strongest_objection: The single strongest bounded objection is that preserved orthogonal intact‑EV signatures in vitro (capture co‑localization, detergent/protease sensitivity, protected‑cargo fingerprint, protein:particle ratio) will not predict recoverable intact‑EV exposure or functional delivery in relevant in vivo contexts—particularly larger species and intranasal administration—so passing the proposed stability gates would not ensure translational delivery or potency (i.e., the attributes are not predictive of the main clinical/PK/PD failure mode).
